candidates.context: 21 CFR 314.94. BE to the RLD may be demonstrated via comparative assessments of the test product to the designated reference standard. See, e.g., 21 CFR 314.3(b) (defining reference standard ). 5 A reference listed drug “is the listed drug identified by FDA as the drug product upon which an applicant relies in seeking approval of its ANDA” (21 CFR 314.3(b)). A reference standard, which is selected by FDA, is the specific drug product that the ANDA applicant must use in conducting any in vivo bioequivalence testing required to support approval of its ANDA (see § 314.3(b)). We recommend that the reference standard also be used for in vitro testing.

candidates.statement: vasoconstrictor BE study. The results of the pilot vasoconstrictor study provide the dose duration-response information necessary to determine the parameters ED50, the dose duration equal to approximately 0.5 times the population ED50 (D1), and the dose duration equal to approximately two times the population ED50 for the simple maximal effect (Emax) model used (D2) to be used in the prospective applicant’s pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study. Development and validation of a suitably sensitive and discriminating region of a dose duration-response standard curve is essential to estimate ED50, D1, and D2 for a vasoconstrictor response. This approach is analogous to using a standard curve to characterize the linearity, range, and limits of quantification for a bioanalytical method for a drug in a biological fluid. The pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study should be performed under the same conditions as the pilot vasoconstrictor study for each topical corticosteroid under investigation.

candidates.statement: A. Vasoconstrictor Method Qualification The chromameter is the apparatus most commonly used to measure the pharmacodynamic skin blanching (small vessel vasoconstriction) response induced following the application of topical corticosteroids. Prior to collecting data for vasoconstrictor studies, the chromameter should be calibrated and qualified for its intended use. In addition, the repeatability and ruggedness 10 of chromameter measurements by different operators should be qualified. These qualifications should be completed before the start of a study. If studies have multiple groups, method qualifications should be performed, at a minimum, before the start date of the first group.
candidates.context: III. PHARMACODYNAMIC VASOCONSTRICTOR STUDIES 1. Chromameter Qualification Chromameter qualification is conducted with calibrated chromameters to support a demonstration of the ruggedness of the chromameter measurements across multiple chromameter units. Multiple chromameter units can be set up to measure the vasoconstrictor response in both the pilot dose duration vasoconstrictor response study and the pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study.

candidates.statement: All chromameters used in these pilot and pivotal vasoconstrictor studies should be reported with their specific identification numbers and qualified to ensure consistent performance in study data collection. Chromameter qualification should be performed on all chromameters planned to be used in pilot and pivotal vasoconstrictor studies using one operator and one subject and with at least four readings each at one designated skin site. Intrachromameter variability is calculated as the variability within multiple readings at one skin site by one operator using one chromameter.

candidates.statement: B. Dose Duration-Response Model The conditions under which the pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study is performed should be optimized to assure that the test topical corticosteroid and RS are compared in the sensitive (steep) portion of the response curve, where the vasoconstrictor response would be sensitive and discriminating to differences in the bioavailability of the corticosteroid between the test topical corticosteroid and RS. Development of a dose duration-response relationship for a topical corticosteroid relies on consistent administration of a predetermined dose of the drug product to the skin. Development of a dose duration-response relationship for a topical corticosteroid will identify the sensitive dose duration-response region to support pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study design. In principle, the time course of the response should be measured until it trends toward baseline to ensure that at each dose duration, the maximal pharmacodynamic response is observed.

candidates.statement: The in vivo vasoconstrictor response (detected as skin blanching) generally approaches a maximum when the dermal vasculature is not able to vasoconstrict further. At relatively high strengths for highly potent topical corticosteroids, there may be a diminishing change in the vasoconstrictor response to increases in dose duration (flattening the response curve at the upper end). Conversely, at relatively low strengths for low potency topical corticosteroids, it may be challenging to elicit a vasoconstrictor response despite increases in dose duration (flattening the response curve at the lower end). Therefore, a prospective applicant should design the pilot vasoconstrictor study to cover a full dose duration-response curve appropriately according to the potency of topical corticosteroids, and, hence, improve the dose duration-response model.
candidates.context: Error models selection. Initial estimates procedure. 11 Dose duration-response data modeled using a nonlinear mixed effect modeling method to determine the population ED50 value. This will serve as the approximate dose duration for the pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study.

candidates.context: 2. Pivotal Vasoconstrictor BE Study This pharmacodynamic BE study uses replicates of single-dose duration of test topical corticosteroid and RS based on the population ED50 identified in the pilot vasoconstrictor study. For a BE analysis, selection of an individual subject is based upon an acceptable ratio of mean reference AUEC at D2 over mean reference AUEC at D1 for each subject. The minimum value of the ratio should be 1.25 and both mean AUEC values at D1 and D2 should be negative, 13 if a simple Emax model is proposed. However, other values for the ratio can be used with justification depending on the selected dose duration-response model. Each individual subject who meets this dose duration-response criterion (under conditions when both mean AUEC at D1 and D2 values are negative) is defined as a detector (i.e., evaluable subject).

It is the applicant’s responsibility to design an adequately powered pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study. FDA recommends that applicants enroll a sufficient number of subjects to yield a number of detectors sufficient to power the study. When determining the sample size of enrolled subjects, dropouts and estimated required number of detectors should be taken into consideration. Based on observations from studies submitted in ANDAs, 40 or more detectors are generally used for the pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study. The sample size determination for the pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study should be prespecified in the protocol and justified.

candidates.statement: Inclusion of nonresponders reduces the ability of a study to detect true differences between the test topical corticosteroid and RS, should they exist. Therefore, for both the pilot vasoconstrictor study and the pivotal vasoconstrictor BE study, only responders should be included for the enrollment.
candidates.context: Quantification of skin blanching in the pilot and pivotal vasoconstrictor studies by a chromameter is considered to be the most satisfactory response measurement. However, responder status may be based on visual readings with the discrete multiple-unit scale (0 to 3 or 0 to 4). A dose duration of 4 hours or 6 hours is suggested, with skin blanching assessment following drug product removal (e.g., 2 hours after drug product removal), but dose duration could vary based on potency of the drug product. A responder shows a visual reading of at least one unit. To conserve skin sites on the ventral forearm for use in the dose duration-response study or BE study, responder status may be based on studies conducted at sites other than the forearm (e.g., upper arm).
